Pragmatism

PRAG-muh-tiz-um -- from Greek pragma, 'a deed, a thing done': a belief in doing what works. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Pragmatism is a belief in practical action and in what actually works.

Pragmatism, not idealism, is what keeps a hospital running through a long night.

Worked Example

With ten minutes left and no money for printing, a student council drops its plan for glossy posters and writes the announcement across the cafeteria whiteboard instead.

Choosing what will actually work over what would be ideal is exactly what pragmatism means. Unlike laziness, pragmatism still aims squarely at the goal -- it just takes the road that exists.

How Pragmatism Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

realism

realism: seeing things as they actually are

practicality

practicality: a focus on what can actually be done

expedience

expedience: choosing whatever gets results, whether or not it is ideal

Antonyms

idealism

idealism: holding out for the perfect solution

fantasy

fantasy: a plan or hope with no basis in reality

How Strong Is It? — realism → pragmatism → expedience

realism vs. pragmatism

realism vs. pragmatism: Realism is quieter than pragmatism -- realism is simply seeing the situation clearly, while pragmatism takes the next step and acts on what will work.

expedience vs. pragmatism

expedience vs. pragmatism: Expedience is pragmatism with the brakes off: pragmatism chooses the practical path, while expedience chooses whatever produces results fastest, even if principles get left behind.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — pragmat-

root — pragmat-: deed, act, a thing done (Greek (pragma, from prassein 'to do'))

suffix — -ism

suffix — -ism: a belief system or practice (Greek (-ismos))

Put it together

Put it together: Greek pragma meant 'a deed, a thing done,' and -ism names a belief -- pragmatism is literally 'the belief in doing,' from the same root that gives us pragmatic and practice.

Use the root in a new word: pragmatic

Use the root in a new word: pragmatic: Her pragmatic solution was to reuse the old wiring rather than wait six months for new.
